messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the canary we ran today, a few embedding-heavy queries blew up with OOM while the embedding matrix was streaming in from sharded safetensors. Need a concrete follow-up for the loader ABI.
kevin: ugh. can you paste the error / logs?
maria: short log: 
```
OOM: failed to allocate 512MB for embedding shard 3/12 during request
hotplug: attempted fallback streaming, but KV cache race caused double map
```
kevin: hmm looks like we raced on mmap + streaming fallback. we should either reserve a tiny staging region or serialize hotplug per-model during on-demand loads.
sylvia: +1. also saw weird alignment when a quantized chunk crossed page boundaries — mmap returns a larger mapping and we tried to write into it.
tom: proposal: introduce a WeightFetchPolicy enum and attach to model manifest. values: INDEX_FIRST, RESERVE_STAGING, STREAM_ONLY, LAZY_PREFETCH. loader will honor policy per namespace.
maria: nice. concrete semantics? INDEX_FIRST = download small index & header metadata, prefetch hot rows (top-k), then stream rest async. RESERVE_STAGING = pre-alloc fixed slab to hydrate into (prevent double-mmap). STREAM_ONLY = never mmap, purely read chunks into ephemeral buffers. LAZY_PREFETCH = take first request path, prefetch incrementally.
aj: question: how do we negotiate this across Dedicated and Private where we can't rely on central CDN hints? need compat if manifest doesn't have policy.
kevin: default should be INDEX_FIRST for most embedding models; legacy bundles without policy default to STREAM_ONLY for safety. we should add a feature flag to Dedicated to force RESERVE_STAGING for customers with strict latency SLAs.
sylvia: we should also add an ABI hook: loader.can_reserve(size) -> bool. if false, fallback to STREAM_ONLY. that avoids OOM.
maria: yes. sample config (manifest snippet):
```
"weight_fetch_policy": "INDEX_FIRST",
"staging_size_bytes": 134217728  # optional, only for RESERVE_STAGING
```
tom: ops-bot can we get a telemetry event for "weight_fetch_policy_chosen" + outcome (success / fallback / oom) so we can measure defaults?
ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-742: add telemetry event + per-model histogram for "fetch_policy" outcome. ETA 2 sprints. :white_check_mark:
kevin: runtime-side tradeoffs: INDEX_FIRST increases tail of first request by ~30-50ms for index download but reduces OOM and gives deterministic prefetch targets. RESERVE_STAGING uses more reserved RAM but makes loads atomic. STREAM_ONLY has lowest startup RAM but highest OOM risk under concurrency.
aj: does INDEX_FIRST require extra manifest fields for per-layer offsets? or can we use compact index (list of chunk byte ranges)?
maria: prefer compact index: list of chunk_n -> {offset,length,quant_meta_tag}. keep it tiny. we already produce small sidecar indices for some formats.
sylvia: another edge: compressed shards (zstd). streaming + index-first for compressed requires server-side decompress streams; need to ensure prefetch decompress threads are limited. otherwise we blow CPU.
tom: ok action items: 1) design WeightFetchPolicy enum and semantics (maria, kevin) 2) add loader.can_reserve(size) hook + fallback path (sylvia) 3) manifest schema update with weight_fetch_policy + compact index (maria) 4) telemetry event + release gating (ops-bot) 5) Dedicated feature flag for forced RESERVE_STAGING (kevin).
maria: timeline: aim for RFC follow-up PR by next week, prototype in runtime repo in 2 weeks.
kevin: I'll sketch the enum and compatibility rules in the RFC doc.
sylvia: I'll prototype can_reserve and a small test harness that simulates concurrent hotplugs.
aj: will run a few customer overlay sims for Dedicated to estimate extra memory cost.
maria: thanks all. if anyone sees a scenario this misses, ping me. also thinking of adding a short fail-open policy: if reserve fails and customer SLA = high, we should surface a clear error rather than try to stream and OOM — prefer predictable failure.
kevin: agreed, explicit failure is better than silent retries. :thumbsup:
maria: final note: doc link draft: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/weight-fetch-policy (WIP)
sylvia: reading now. good writeup so far.
